title: Write the monospace rule to a conf.d drop-in, not fonts.conf
head: d901651ff792
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: An unreadable fonts.conf or failed awk can delete the user's entire file
leads.consequence: With a regular fonts.conf whose parent directory is writable but the file is not readable, mktemp makes an empty sibling, awk fails, cmp differs, the grep pipeline finds no content, and rm removes both the temp and the original. The caller does not inspect any command's exit status, and can continue to restart the shell. The same deletion is possible when awk fails for other reasons, including read errors. In the mktemp-failure case an empty legacy_tmp similarly feeds the empty-content branch, although unlinking requires a writable parent.

leads.summary: A user-created monospace prepend_first rule is indistinguishable from generated content and is deleted
leads.consequence: A user fonts.conf consisting of a legitimate <match target="pattern"> block with <string>monospace</string> and mode="prepend_first" is removed altogether, regardless of who wrote it, the value being prepended, or whether it has extra edits or a comment inside the block. In a mixed file the entire matching user block is silently stripped. Preservation of user-authored overrides cannot be inferred from the structure alone.

leads.summary: XML-equivalent legacy rule formatting escapes the exact-text remover and still overrides the new choice
leads.consequence: A fonts.conf with <match  target="pattern">, <match target='pattern'>, or <match target="pattern" > is accepted as XML but never satisfies /<match target="pattern">/. The old prepend_first stays in fonts.conf after the new drop-in is written, so the user's fontconfig family order can still prefer the old name. The same holds for spelling variants of mode='prepend_first'. Do not claim every legacy block is removed.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (gen_single_quoted_target); concerns user-reformatted blocks

leads.summary: Changed fonts.conf symlinks and permissions are replaced by a 0600 temporary file
leads.consequence: When any block is removed, mv replaces the symlink itself rather than editing its referent; a configuration-manager-managed link or shared target is disconnected. For a regular file, mktemp's mode 0600 becomes the new fonts.conf mode after mv; non-default ACLs and ownership metadata are not copied. This also occurs for ordinary user files if awk merely adds a trailing newline to an existing no-final-newline file. The drop-in itself is still written separately.

leads.summary: Failure to create the drop-in is not propagated before legacy cleanup
leads.consequence: If ~/.config/fontconfig/conf.d is unwritable or mkdir/cat fails, the script still processes or deletes legacy fonts.conf, runs the shell restart, and can report success via its last hook. The requested font never reaches fontconfig; if the old generated rule was deleted, fontconfig falls back to the packaged default. Gate writing and cleanup on a successful drop-in write.
leads.triage: behavioural; unchecked-write pattern pre-exists in base, low impact; not sent to Opus

leads.summary: Style stops watching user fonts.conf, and cannot catch creation when conf.d was missing at startup
leads.consequence: Manual edits to the still-effective ~/.config/fontconfig/fonts.conf no longer invoke resolveFontFamily; the gallery's Style.font.resolvedFamily can stay stale until shell restart. The upstream FileView implementation watches the target plus its immediate parent only: on a fresh user with no conf.d yet, starting the shell and later manually creating conf.d/50-omarchy-monospace.conf cannot produce a watch event, although using font set normally restarts the shell. With an existing parent directory and missing file, the upstream source does handle file creation. Keep a watcher for both effective files or watch an existing ancestor / provide an explicit reload.

leads.summary: Two match elements on one line are discarded together, removing unrelated user rules
leads.consequence: A valid fonts.conf can have an Omarchy-generated monospace <match> followed on the same line by a user's rgba or serif <match>. The first awk rule tests the whole input line, sees the legacy three substrings, and prints none of the line. The user's second block is lost; if this was the whole file, the later empty-output test unlinks it entirely. The test's mixed-file fixture puts the user block on a separate line, so it does not exercise this case.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (N2 minified/one-line cases)

leads.summary: Open PR #12935's mixed-file test conflicts with this cleaner
leads.consequence: If both changes and their tests merge without reconciliation, #12935's case 4 asserts fonts.conf remains byte-identical even when it contains a legacy-looking monospace rule and a user serif rule, while this PR removes the mono block. That test fails. Decide the intended preservation contract and update the exact assertion or the cleanup strategy; #12935 also adds a one-shot migration for old font selection and both PRs change bin/omarchy-font-set and Style.qml.
leads.triage: factual, verified by coordinator (coord/12935-test.sh lines 75-95) and Opus self-check

leads.summary: Open PR #12969's font-set test requires the retired fonts.conf output
leads.consequence: Both PRs add a test/shell.d/font-set-test.sh at the same path. #12969 checks -f ~/.config/fontconfig/fonts.conf immediately after font set, while this PR writes only conf.d/... and never creates fonts.conf; simply merging both feature changes without rewriting the fixture makes the #12969 test fail and creates an add/add test-file conflict. Adapt its first-family assertions to the drop-in before merging.

leads.summary: Open PR #12457's escaping test checks the old output path
leads.consequence: If #12457's escaping fix and its test are merged with this PR, its clean fake HOME contains no fonts.conf and its last assertion greps precisely that now-unwritten path, causing a test failure despite the font family being escaped into the conf.d drop-in. Update that assertion to ~/.config/fontconfig/conf.d/50-omarchy-monospace.conf in #12457's new test.
leads.triage: factual, file list verified; minor integration detail

limits: Source-only hunt: no review.py-run execution or fontconfig/Quickshell runtime launch. Assertions above are derived from pinned script and fetched upstream source; file modes, shell exit status and effective font order are not runtime measurements.

The Quickshell FileView source is the public upstream master snapshot fetched under deps/quickshell, not a separately pinned Arch quickshell package revision; the missing-directory scenario should be checked against the distribution's shipped source before presenting it as an installed-version guarantee.
Other related PRs modify bin/omarchy-font-set (including #12999 and #13235), but no further verified behavioral collision beyond the specifically cited incompatible tests was established.

flags.claim: #12927 suggests ... and a backup at minimum.
flags.why: Lost qualifier. #12927 offers the backup as the minimum only as an alternative: 'If the drop-in move is unwanted, then at minimum back the file up the way omarchy refresh does rather than truncating in place.' It is not paired with the block-stripping migration.

flags.claim: the result is the silent loss #12927 is about
flags.why: Minor. The command exits 0 and nothing says fonts.conf was removed, but on the CLI stderr shows the underlying errors: the mktemp message plus 'line 83: : No such file or directory' and 'grep: : No such file or directory'; the gawk 'error writing standard output' warning; or 'awk: fatal: cannot open file ... Permission denied'. From the font menu no output is visible.

flags.claim: #12935's test requires a mixed fonts.conf containing a generated-style block to stay byte-identical
flags.why: Minor. #12935 compares [[ $(cat "$user_fonts_conf") == "$mixed_rule" ]], and command substitution strips trailing newlines, so the test requires the content to be unchanged apart from trailing newlines, not byte-identical. The 'opposite contract' conclusion stands: its Case 4 file (the generated-style monospace block plus a one-line serif prepend_first rule) must be unchanged, while this PR removes the monospace block.

Prevalence judgement with no evidence. My report says frequency is unknown and only calls the N2 formatting uncommon. It is acceptable because the sentence immediately hedges ('how often they occur is unknown'), but the two halves pull against each other.
Outside my evidence: I cannot observe my own effort setting, and I did not observe the Sol or editorial runs. The coordinator verifies this with subagents, pi_job verify and check-result.

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

Follow-up to the [earlier review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/13092#issuecomment-5825959795) and the [author's reply](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/13092#issuecomment-5833494400), checked at d901651f.

**Verified:** the earlier finding is resolved for the inputs it described. A generated block mixed with user rules, a comment, a trailing blank line, CRLF line endings or a one-line block is now removed, the user's other rules are kept, and the chosen font is first for `monospace`. The `Style.qml` comment and watched path now name the drop-in. The new mixed-file test fails on the previously reviewed head and passes on this one.

**Correction to the earlier review:** it suggested removing only the generated block "as #12927 suggests". That attribution was wrong. #12927 suggests stripping the block from `fonts.conf` only "when that is all it contains, and leave the file alone otherwise" (what the previous commit did), with a backup as the fallback if the drop-in move was unwanted. Block removal was the earlier review's own suggestion.

The block removal adds new ways to lose parts of `fonts.conf` that the previous commit did not have. Details follow.

### A failed `mktemp` or `awk` deletes `fonts.conf`

In `bin/omarchy-font-set`, neither the `mktemp` nor the `awk` exit status is checked. An empty temp file then passes the "only the XML skeleton is left" check:

```text
mktemp fails (disk full) or awk cannot read/write
  -> legacy_tmp is "" or an empty file
  -> grep finds no non-skeleton line
  -> rm -f "$legacy_tmp" "$legacy_fontconfig"      # user's fonts.conf deleted, exit 0
```

Reproduced in a sandbox with a user-only `fonts.conf` (an rgba rule, no generated block): a `mktemp` stub exiting 1, gawk output limited by `ulimit -f 0`, and a `fonts.conf` with mode 000. The file was deleted in all three and the command exited 0. The previously reviewed head kept the file byte-identical in all three.

**Impact:** low likelihood (full disk or quota, an unreadable file), but the result is the loss #12927 is about, with exit 0 and nothing saying the file was removed. A user whose `fonts.conf` holds no Omarchy content at all can lose it.

**Suggested change:** skip the cleanup when `mktemp` or `awk` fails, and delete `fonts.conf` only when a block was actually removed and the remainder is the skeleton.

### The block filter also removes content that is not the generated block

The filter is line-based and matches on three substrings anywhere in a block. Results on synthetic files, with fontconfig 2.18.3:

| `fonts.conf` content | Previous head (fb8a0be0) | This head |
|---|---|---|
| User rule scoped to kitty (`prgname`) with monospace `prepend_first` | kept | removed; `monospace` for kitty's program name resolves to the global font instead of the user's |
| User rule mapping `Consolas` to monospace with `prepend_first` | kept | removed, file deleted |
| User-only file with a comment such as `<!-- TODO: a <match target="font"> rule later -->`, then an `<alias>` | kept | file deleted |
| `</match><match target="font">` on one line, plus the generated block | kept | malformed XML; fontconfig then drops every rule in the file |
| Whole file on one line (rgba rule plus generated block) | kept | file deleted |

A line that opens `<match…>` without closing it (including inside a comment) starts a buffer that is dropped at the next `<match` line or never printed at end of file. #12927 lists `prgname` scopes among the things users keep in this file.

**Impact:** rules the user wrote are silently removed, or the whole file is deleted, with no Omarchy content involved in some cases. These file shapes are probably uncommon; how often they occur is unknown.

**Suggested change:** remove a block only when it matches the generated template exactly (the eight lines earlier versions wrote, with the font name masked), which is the previous commit's normalisation applied per block. Flush the buffer at end of file and before starting a new one. A backup of `fonts.conf` before modifying or deleting it, as `omarchy refresh` does, would make any remaining case recoverable.

### Minor notes

- **File replacement:** every rewrite goes through `mktemp` and `mv`, so the file becomes mode 0600, and a symlinked `fonts.conf` (dotfiles managers) is replaced by a regular file while the linked copy keeps the old block. A user file without a final newline is rewritten even when nothing was removed. The same script already uses `sed --follow-symlinks` for `kitty.conf`.
- **Optional test improvement:** the "Style.qml watches the fontconfig drop-in" check greps for a path that the new comment also contains, so it still passes with the `FileView` path reverted to `fonts.conf`. Anchoring the grep on the `path:` line would make it meaningful.
- **Watch:** `Style.qml` now watches only the drop-in, so hand edits to `fonts.conf`, whose rules still apply after the drop-in, no longer trigger a live re-resolve until the shell restarts. Watching both paths would keep both.
- **PR description:** it still says the user's `fonts.conf` "is left completely alone", but the script now edits and can delete it.
- **Related open PRs:** #12935 takes the same drop-in approach, and its test requires a mixed `fonts.conf` containing a generated-style block to stay unchanged, the opposite contract. #12969 adds a different `test/shell.d/font-set-test.sh`.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Source review of the new commit, the previous head, the base and #12927, plus fontconfig 2.18.3 include order, rule handling and parse-error handling, and Quickshell `FileView` source. Isolated runs used synthetic `fonts.conf` files against the head, the previous head, the first commit and the base, with stubbed Omarchy commands and a synthetic fontconfig 2.18.3 configuration with no installed fonts, comparing family lists from `fc-pattern`. Disk-full cases were simulated with a failing `mktemp` stub and `ulimit -f 0`. Not tested: a live desktop session, a real full disk, installed fonts through `fc-match`, and other fontconfig versions.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.

**Opt out:** To stop receiving these reviews, reply to this comment saying so.
